consents.title: Telehealth Informed Consent
consents.body:
DRAFT — pending Dr. Om and Offit Kurman counsel approval. Not for use until approved.

Version 1.0 — DRAFT, November 9, 2026, pending approval

Please read this consent carefully. It explains how UNZIT provides care, what online care can and cannot do, and what we ask of you. You will be asked to accept this document before treatment. Your acceptance is recorded with the version you accepted.

1. What UNZIT is

UNZIT is an online dermatology service for acne, operated by The Derm Guy LLC dba UNZIT. UNZIT treats acne only, and only in adults age 18 and older. UNZIT provides care by store-and-forward telehealth. That means you answer written questions and send photos, and the clinician reviews them later and responds in the app. There is no live video visit, no phone visit, and no real-time conversation.

2. Who provides your care

Your treating clinician is Amit Om, MD, a dermatologist (North Carolina medical license number 022-00012). Dr. Om personally reviews your intake answers and photos, decides your treatment plan, and sends any prescriptions. If Dr. Om decides your condition needs in-person care, or is not suited to online treatment, he will tell you and recommend in-person care.

3. How care works

1. You complete an intake questionnaire and upload the required photos.

2. You verify your identity and confirm your location (sections 6 and 7).

3. Dr. Om reviews your case within 1 to 2 business days and responds in the app with a treatment plan, a message, a request for more information or better photos, or a recommendation for in-person care.

4. Follow-up happens the same way: you send photos and answers, and Dr. Om reviews them within 1 to 2 business days. UNZIT is not monitored around the clock. Messages are answered during the review window above, not immediately.

4. Not for emergencies

UNZIT is not for emergencies and does not provide urgent or emergency care. If you have an emergency, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department now. Emergencies include trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, chest pain, fainting, a severe headache with vision changes, or a blistering or rapidly spreading rash. Do not wait for an app reply in an emergency.

5. Limits of online care

Online care has limits you should understand before you consent:

1. Dr. Om cannot examine your skin in person, touch it, or use in-office instruments or tests. Diagnosis rests on your answers and your photos.

2. Photos can miss detail because of lighting, focus, or skin tone rendering. Poor photos can delay your case, and Dr. Om may ask for new photos before deciding.

3. Some conditions that look like acne are not acne, and some acne needs in-person procedures, lab work, or medicines UNZIT does not offer. Dr. Om may refer you for in-person care at any point.

4. Treatment may not work, may work slowly, or may cause side effects. No result is promised or guaranteed.

5. Technology can fail. App, internet, or device problems can delay a review or a message. If something seems wrong, contact us at hello@tryunzit.com.

6. You must be in North Carolina

You must be physically located in North Carolina when you submit your intake, when you receive care, and at each follow-up check-in. UNZIT confirms this by your attestation in the app. If you are outside North Carolina, do not submit a case or check-in; Dr. Om cannot treat you there at this time.

7. Identity verification

Before care, you must verify your identity by uploading a government photo ID (driver license, state ID, or passport) and taking a live selfie. The name and date of birth on the ID must match your account, the selfie must match the ID photo, and you must be 18 or older. Dr. Om reviews your identity before care. Care provided to anyone using another person's identity or account is not permitted, and UNZIT may end care if information you provide is false.

8. Your answers must be complete and accurate

Your safety depends on your answers. You agree to:

1. Answer every intake and follow-up question fully and truthfully, including your medical conditions, allergies, and every medicine, vitamin, and supplement you use.

2. Tell UNZIT promptly if anything changes, including a new medicine, a new allergy, a new medical condition, or pregnancy, breastfeeding, or plans for pregnancy.

3. Upload photos that are current, unfiltered, and taken as instructed: daylight or bright light, no makeup on the areas photographed, hair pulled back, and each photo sharp and in focus. Never send photos of the genital area or breasts. Chest photos must be above the breasts, and you may cover or crop anything you choose.

9. Prescriptions

1. A prescription is provided only when Dr. Om decides it is clinically appropriate. Subscribing does not guarantee a prescription, a particular medicine, or a refill.

2. Prescriptions are sent electronically through TreatRx (DoseSpot), a separate e-prescribing service outside this app. The app records that a prescription was sent.

3. On the Care plan, your prescription goes to the United States pharmacy you choose, and you pay that pharmacy directly for your medicine. On the All-In plan, prescription cost is included and Vida pharmacy dispenses and ships your medicine to your North Carolina address.

4. UNZIT prescribes non-controlled acne medicines only. UNZIT does not prescribe isotretinoin (Accutane and similar brands) and does not prescribe controlled substances.

5. The separate Medication Consent describes the risks of each medicine and the side effect rule in section 10. You must accept it before any prescription is sent.

10. The side effect rule

If you notice any side effect from a medicine Dr. Om prescribed, even a small one, stop that medication and message UNZIT through the app. Do not restart it until Dr. Om replies. This rule has no exceptions for mild symptoms. If you have any of the emergency symptoms listed in section 4, stop the medication and call 911 or go to an emergency department instead of waiting for a reply.

11. Records, privacy, and sharing for your care

Your intake answers, photos, messages, identity documents, and treatment records are your health information. UNZIT creates and keeps a record of your care. UNZIT may share your information as needed for your treatment, for payment, and to run the service, including with the pharmacy that fills your prescription, the e-prescribing service, and, if you ask, your primary care doctor or another treating clinician. The Privacy Notice explains these uses, your rights, and how your information is protected. Use of your information or photos for marketing requires your separate permission and is never a condition of care.

12. Costs and insurance

UNZIT does not bill insurance, Medicaid, or Medicare, and your subscription is not covered by insurance. You are responsible for your subscription charges under the Subscription Terms. On the Care plan you are also responsible for what your pharmacy charges you. Lab work, in-person visits, procedures, and over-the-counter products are not included in your subscription and are your responsibility if Dr. Om recommends them.

13. Withdrawing consent

You may withdraw your consent to telehealth care at any time in the app or by emailing hello@tryunzit.com. Withdrawing consent ends your care through UNZIT going forward; it does not undo care already provided or cancel charges already incurred. If you withdraw consent, obtain follow-up care from another clinician, especially if you are mid-treatment.

14. Your acceptance

By selecting I ACCEPT, you state that: you have read and understand this consent; you are 18 or older; you will be physically in North Carolina for your care; you agree to care by store-and-forward telehealth with the limits described here; and you agree to the side effect rule in section 10. I ACCEPT.

consents.title: Medication Consent
consents.body:
DRAFT — pending Dr. Om and Offit Kurman counsel approval. Not for use until approved.

Version 1.0 — DRAFT, November 9, 2026, pending approval

Please read this consent carefully before any medicine is prescribed for you. It describes the medicines UNZIT may use for acne, their main risks, and the safety rules that apply to all of them. Dr. Om will choose the medicine or combination he judges right for your skin. You will be asked to accept this document before treatment, and your acceptance is recorded with the version you accepted.

1. Medicines UNZIT may prescribe

Treatment may include one or more of the following:

1. Topical retinoids: tretinoin and tazarotene (creams or gels applied to the skin).

2. Doxycycline (an oral antibiotic in the tetracycline family).

3. Spironolactone (an oral medicine used for hormonal acne in women).

4. Hydroquinone (a cream for dark marks left by acne).

5. Azelaic acid (a cream or gel).

6. Benzoyl peroxide (a wash or gel, prescription or as directed with your prescriptions).

7. Clindamycin (a topical antibiotic, always used together with benzoyl peroxide).

8. Dapsone (a topical gel). UNZIT does not prescribe isotretinoin (Accutane, Absorica, Claravis, and similar brands) and does not prescribe controlled substances.

2. Benefits, alternatives, and no guarantee

These medicines can reduce breakouts, inflammation, and dark marks, but acne treatment is slow. Most medicines take 8 to 12 weeks of steady use before improvement is clear, and some acne does not respond to a given medicine. No benefit is promised or guaranteed. Alternatives to any medicine Dr. Om suggests include a different acne medicine, in-person dermatology care (which can offer procedures, lab monitoring, and medicines UNZIT does not offer, including isotretinoin), over-the-counter products, and no treatment. You may decline any medicine and ask Dr. Om about alternatives through the app at any time.

3. Rules that apply to every medicine

1. Use each medicine exactly as directed on your prescription and in your plan. Do not share your medicine with anyone, and do not use someone else's.

2. Tell Dr. Om about pregnancy, breastfeeding, plans for pregnancy, allergies, medical conditions, and all medicines and supplements you use, before treatment starts and whenever anything changes.

3. Dr. Om may ask you to get lab work or see a clinician in person before or during treatment, for example to check potassium during spironolactone treatment. Lab work and in-person care are not included in your subscription.

4. Stop a non-prescription retinol or adapalene product when Dr. Om starts a prescription retinoid, unless your plan says otherwise. Use one retinoid at a time.

4. The side effect rule

If you notice any side effect, even a small one, stop that medication and message UNZIT through the app. Do not restart it until Dr. Om replies. Do not push through a side effect to see if it goes away. Stop the medication and call 911 or go to an emergency department now if you have: swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; hives; trouble breathing; a severe headache with vision changes; fainting; an irregular heartbeat; or a blistering, peeling, or painful rash. These can be signs of a serious reaction.

5. Pregnancy and breastfeeding

Some acne medicines can harm an unborn baby. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, trying to become pregnant, or not sure, you must tell Dr. Om before treatment and at every check-in. In any of those situations, UNZIT will not prescribe tretinoin, tazarotene, hydroquinone, doxycycline, or spironolactone for you. Treatment options that may still be available include azelaic acid and clindamycin with benzoyl peroxide, as Dr. Om judges appropriate. If you become pregnant while using any medicine from UNZIT, stop it and message UNZIT right away, and tell your obstetric clinician what you were using.

6. Topical retinoids: tretinoin and tazarotene

Retinoids unclog pores, prevent new breakouts, and improve dark marks and skin texture over time. Common effects, especially in the first weeks, are dryness, peeling, redness, stinging, and a temporary increase in breakouts before improvement begins. Retinoids make skin more sensitive to the sun, so daily sunscreen is required while using them, and sunburn risk is higher. Apply a pea-sized amount as directed, usually at night, and use moisturizer to manage dryness. Waxing and harsh scrubs on treated skin can cause injury and should be avoided. Do not use a retinoid if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, trying to become pregnant, or not sure (section 5). Tazarotene is the stronger of the two and causes irritation more often.

7. Doxycycline (oral)

Doxycycline reduces inflammation and bacteria in moderate to severe acne. It is time-limited: Dr. Om reassesses it at about 12 weeks and stops it by about 16 weeks, and it is always combined with benzoyl peroxide and a topical retinoid, which continue after doxycycline stops. Risks and precautions:

1. Sun sensitivity: you can sunburn much more easily, sometimes severely. Use sunscreen daily and limit sun exposure.

2. Stomach and throat injury: nausea, stomach upset, and irritation or ulcer of the esophagus can occur. Take each dose with a full glass of water and food as directed, stay upright for at least 30 minutes after taking it, and do not take it right before bed.

3. Yeast infections, including vaginal yeast infections, can occur with antibiotic use.

4. Rarely, increased pressure inside the skull (pseudotumor cerebri) can occur. A severe headache with vision changes is an emergency (section 4).

5. Interactions: antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, zinc, or magnesium reduce absorption, so separate them from your dose as directed. Tell Dr. Om if you use a blood thinner, lithium, or seizure medicine.

6. Do not use if you are allergic to tetracyclines, or if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, trying to become pregnant, or not sure (section 5), because tetracyclines can harm a baby's developing teeth and bones.

8. Spironolactone (oral, for women)

Spironolactone reduces the hormone effect that drives hormonal acne, usually along the jawline and chin and around periods. It takes 2 to 3 months to judge its effect. Risks and precautions:

1. It is a diuretic and blood pressure medicine at its root, so it can cause increased urination, dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, especially when standing up quickly or at higher doses.

2. It can raise potassium. Raised potassium can affect heart rhythm and may cause no symptoms. Risk is higher if you have kidney disease, adrenal disease, or high potassium, or if you use ACE inhibitor or ARB blood pressure medicines (such as lisinopril or losartan), potassium supplements or salt substitutes, water pills, trimethoprim (Bactrim), or digoxin. Tell Dr. Om if you use any of these. Dr. Om may require lab checks of potassium and kidney function.

3. Breast tenderness and changes in menstrual periods, including irregular periods, are common.

4. Do not use if you are pregnant, trying to become pregnant, or not sure (section 5), because spironolactone can affect the development of a male fetus. Reliable birth control is required while using it if you could become pregnant.

5. Tell Dr. Om if you have or have had kidney disease, liver disease, heart disease or an irregular heartbeat, fainting or very low blood pressure, adrenal disease (Addison disease), or breast cancer. Note: spironolactone for acne is an off-label use. It is approved for other conditions, not for acne (section 13).

9. Hydroquinone

Hydroquinone lightens dark marks left after acne heals. Apply it only to the marks, exactly as directed, once nightly. UNZIT prescribes hydroquinone in courses of up to 12 weeks of nightly use. When a course ends, stop using it; Dr. Om will reassess your marks and, if another course is appropriate, set it at a check-in. Do not use hydroquinone continuously for longer than 12 weeks, and do not extend a course on your own. Between courses, azelaic acid and daily sunscreen maintain your progress. Hydroquinone can cause redness, dryness, stinging, and irritation. With long or unsupervised use it can cause a blue-black or gray darkening of the skin (exogenous ochronosis) that is difficult to reverse, which is why the course limit matters. If you notice blue-black or gray darkening of treated skin, stop the medication and message UNZIT through the app, and do not restart it until Dr. Om replies. Daily sunscreen is required, because sun exposure will darken the marks again and can undo progress. Do not use if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, trying to become pregnant, or not sure (section 5).

10. Azelaic acid

Azelaic acid treats both breakouts and dark marks and is the option most often used when the medicines in section 5 are off the table. It can cause mild burning, tingling, itching, or dryness, which usually lessens with continued use. Serious reactions are uncommon.

11. Benzoyl peroxide and clindamycin

Benzoyl peroxide kills acne bacteria and prevents antibiotic resistance. It can dry and irritate skin, and it bleaches fabric, towels, pillowcases, and hair on contact. Rarely, it causes a true allergy, including swelling; section 4 applies. Topical clindamycin is an antibiotic gel or lotion. Dr. Om always prescribes it together with benzoyl peroxide, because clindamycin used alone quickly stops working as bacteria become resistant. Clindamycin can cause dryness and irritation. Rarely, topical antibiotics are linked to severe diarrhea from a bowel infection (Clostridioides difficile), even weeks after use; tell Dr. Om promptly about severe or bloody diarrhea.

12. Dapsone

Dapsone gel reduces inflamed breakouts. It can cause dryness, redness, peeling, and itching where applied, and it can temporarily turn skin or facial hair orange-brown where it mixes with benzoyl peroxide applied at the same time; apply them at different times of day as directed. Rarely, dapsone can affect the blood (including methemoglobinemia and, in people with G6PD deficiency, breakdown of red blood cells). Tell Dr. Om if you have G6PD deficiency or anemia, and seek urgent care for unusual paleness, blue or gray lips, severe fatigue, or shortness of breath.

13. Off-label uses and compounded medicines

One UNZIT use is off-label, which means the FDA approved the medicine for another condition but not for this one: spironolactone for acne. Off-label prescribing is common and lawful in dermatology, and Dr. Om will tell you when a medicine he prescribes for you is off-label. Some prescriptions may be compounded, meaning a pharmacy prepares them for you individually. Compounded medicines are not FDA approved, and their strength and purity are not verified by the FDA the way manufactured medicines are.

14. Your acceptance

By selecting I ACCEPT, you state that: you have read and understand the benefits, risks, and alternatives described here, including the pregnancy rules in section 5 and the side effect rule in section 4; you have told, or will tell before treatment, Dr. Om about pregnancy and breastfeeding status, allergies, medical conditions, and all medicines and supplements you use; and you agree to stop any medicine at any side effect, however minor, and message UNZIT, and not restart until Dr. Om replies. I ACCEPT.

consents.title: Privacy Notice
consents.body:
DRAFT — pending Dr. Om and Offit Kurman counsel approval. Not for use until approved.

Version 1.0 — DRAFT, November 9, 2026, pending approval

Effective date: November 30, 2026.

UNZIT is operated by The Derm Guy LLC dba UNZIT. This notice describes how your health information may be used and shared, and how you can access it, as provided under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and North Carolina law. We are required by law to maintain the privacy of your protected health information, to give you this notice, and to follow the terms of the notice currently in effect. Please read it carefully. You will be asked to acknowledge that you received it.

1. Information we collect

1. Identity and contact information: your name, date of birth, email address, and account details, plus the government photo ID and live selfie you provide to verify identity.

2. Health information: your intake answers, follow-up answers, photos of your skin, messages with Dr. Om, diagnoses, treatment plans, and prescription records.

3. Payment information: collected and processed by Stripe, our payment processor. We do not store your full card number.

4. Device and usage information: basic technical information needed to run and secure the app, such as device type, app activity, and security logs.

5. Website and waitlist information: if you join the waitlist, we keep your email, state, and answers for launch notices. Do not send health information through the website form; health information belongs in the app after you create an account.

2. How we use your information

We use your health information mainly to treat you: Dr. Om reviews it, plans your treatment, prescribes, and follows up. We also use it to run the service, including scheduling reviews, processing payment through Stripe, communicating with you, maintaining your record, quality review, and meeting legal obligations. Email about your care is sent through Paubox, a service designed for health information. Please also keep health details inside the app rather than ordinary email where you can.

3. When we share your information

We share the minimum information reasonably needed for each purpose:

1. For your treatment: with the pharmacy that fills your prescription (Vida pharmacy on the All-In plan, or the pharmacy you choose on the Care plan), with TreatRx (DoseSpot), the e-prescribing service that transmits your prescription, and with other treating clinicians. If you ask us to send a summary of your plan to your primary care doctor, we will do so with your permission.

2. With service providers: companies that run parts of UNZIT for us, such as cloud hosting, email, database, photo storage, and e-prescribing providers. Providers that handle health information for us act as our business associates and do so under business associate agreements requiring them to protect it and use it only for our purposes. Our current health information providers under signed business associate agreements include Google (Google Cloud and Google Workspace) and Paubox.

3. As required or permitted by law: for example, in response to a court order, as part of a regulatory investigation or action, for public health or health oversight activities, or to avert a serious threat to health or safety.

4. With your written authorization: for any other purpose, including any marketing use of your information or photos. Marketing use always requires your separate permission, and you can revoke it. We do not sell your health information. There are no advertising pixels in the logged-in app or the intake.

4. Your photos

Your treatment photos are part of your health record and are treated as private health information. Location metadata is removed from uploaded images. Do not send photos of the genital area or breasts; chest photos must be above the breasts.

5. How we protect your information

We use administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect your information, including access controls that limit records to the people and systems providing your care, secure transmission, and vendors selected for health data handling under business associate agreements where applicable. No system is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security of your information. If a breach of your unsecured health information occurs, we will notify you as HIPAA requires.

6. Your rights

You have the right to:

1. See and get a copy of your health information, usually within 30 days of your request. We may charge a reasonable, cost-based fee where the law allows.

2. Ask us to correct (amend) information you believe is wrong or incomplete. If we decline, we will tell you why in writing, and you may add a statement of disagreement.

3. Get a list (an accounting) of certain disclosures of your health information made during the six years before your request, excluding disclosures for treatment, payment, and operations and disclosures you authorized.

4. Ask us to limit how we use or share your information (a restriction request). We are not required to agree to every request, except that we must agree not to disclose information to a health plan about an item or service you paid for in full out of pocket, if you ask. UNZIT does not bill health plans, so if we decline a restriction we will tell you.

5. Ask us to contact you in a specific way or at a specific address (confidential communications), for example only through the app or only at a certain email address. We will agree to reasonable requests.

6. Get a paper or electronic copy of this notice at any time, even if you acknowledged it electronically.

7. Choose someone to act for you, such as a medical power of attorney or legal guardian, who can exercise your rights and make choices about your information.

8. Be notified if a breach occurs that may have compromised the privacy or security of your information. To use any of these rights, contact the Privacy Officer, The Derm Guy LLC dba UNZIT, at hello@tryunzit.com or by mail at 1235 East Blvd, Ste. E #1107, Charlotte, NC 28203.

7. How long we keep records

We keep your health record for 11 years after your last visit, as medical records must be retained and may be needed for your future care.

8. Changes to this notice

We may change this notice, and the changes will apply to all health information we hold about you. If we make a material change, we will post the revised notice in the app with a new version and effective date before the change takes effect where the law requires, and your continued care under the revised notice will be recorded in the app.

9. Complaints

If you believe your privacy rights have been violated, you may complain to us at hello@tryunzit.com, or to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights. We will not retaliate against you for filing a complaint.

10. Your acknowledgment

By selecting I ACKNOWLEDGE, you confirm that this Privacy Notice was made available to you and that you had the chance to read it before treatment. Acknowledgment is not consent to any use that requires your separate written authorization. I ACKNOWLEDGE.

consents.title: Subscription Terms
consents.body:
DRAFT — pending Dr. Om and Offit Kurman counsel approval. Not for use until approved.

Version 1.0 — DRAFT, November 9, 2026, pending approval

These terms describe your UNZIT subscription: the two plans, what each includes, how billing and renewal work, and how to cancel. UNZIT is operated by The Derm Guy LLC dba UNZIT. You will be asked to agree to these terms at checkout, and your agreement is recorded with the version you accepted.

1. The plans and prices

UNZIT has two monthly plans:

1. Care: $39 per month.

2. All-In: $89 per month. The price charged is the price shown for your selected plan at checkout. Both plans provide the same clinical care by Dr. Amit Om, a dermatologist: review of your intake and photos, a treatment plan, prescriptions when clinically appropriate, follow-up check-ins, and messaging through the app. The plans differ in how prescriptions are paid for and filled (section 2). Care is reviewed within 1 to 2 business days; that response window applies to both plans.

2. What each plan includes, and how prescriptions work

1. Care ($39 per month): Dr. Om sends any prescription to the United States pharmacy you choose. You pay that pharmacy directly for your medicine. Prescription prices are set by your pharmacy and are not included in your subscription.

2. All-In ($89 per month): the cost of prescriptions Dr. Om prescribes for you is included when they are filled by Vida pharmacy. Vida dispenses your medicine and ships it to your North Carolina address. Prescriptions filled anywhere else are at your own cost.

3. Check-ins: your treatment plan includes follow-up photo check-ins and brief questions, which you complete in the app. On the Care plan, check-ins are monthly. On the All-In plan, check-ins are weekly for the first eight weeks after clinical approval, then monthly.

4. Not included in either plan: over-the-counter products (including any benzoyl peroxide, cleanser, moisturizer, or sunscreen your plan recommends buying), in-person visits or procedures, lab work, and medicines outside the UNZIT acne formulary. If Dr. Om recommends any of these, they are at your own cost.

5. A prescription is never guaranteed. Dr. Om prescribes only when clinically appropriate, and UNZIT does not prescribe isotretinoin or controlled substances.

3. Who may subscribe

You must be 18 or older to subscribe and receive care. UNZIT treats acne only, and only while you are physically in North Carolina (see the Telehealth Informed Consent). You subscribe and receive care for yourself only, under your own verified identity. If you are found ineligible before payment, for example because of your age, location, or condition, you are not charged.

4. Billing and automatic renewal

1. Payment is processed by Stripe (Stripe Checkout). Your billing period starts at payment.

2. Your subscription renews automatically each month at the then-current price for your plan, charged to your payment method on file through Stripe, until you cancel. By subscribing, you authorize these recurring charges.

3. Keep your payment method current. If a charge fails, Stripe may retry it, and your access to reviews, messaging, and prescriptions may pause until payment succeeds.

4. UNZIT does not bill insurance, Medicaid, or Medicare, and subscription charges are not reimbursable by UNZIT if your insurer declines to cover them.

5. Cancellation and refunds

1. You may cancel at any time through the Stripe Customer Portal, which is also where you update payment details and change plans. You do not need to call or email to cancel.

2. Cancellation stops future renewals. It takes effect at the end of the paid period: your current paid month continues in full, including reviews, messaging, and, on All-In, shipments already scheduled within that period, and you keep access until that period ends.

3. Amounts already paid are not refunded, including for a partially used month, except as stated in item 4 below and where the law requires otherwise.

4. If your case is rejected at clinical review and Dr. Om decides not to treat you, your latest paid invoice is refunded in full and your subscription is cancelled immediately.

5. Medicines already shipped cannot be returned to the pharmacy.

6. Changing plans

You may change between Care and All-In in the Stripe Customer Portal. Plan changes are prorated immediately through Stripe: you are charged or credited the difference for the remainder of the period. A proration credit is applied to future charges and is not a cash refund. If you move from All-In to Care, prescription coverage through Vida ends when the change takes effect, and later fills are at your own cost at your chosen pharmacy.

7. Price changes

If we change plan prices, we will notify you by email before the new price applies to you. The new price takes effect from the first renewal after the notice. If you do not agree to a new price, cancel through the Stripe Customer Portal before that renewal; cancelling follows section 5.

8. What happens to prescriptions when your subscription ends

1. A prescription already sent remains with the pharmacy. On the Care plan, whether the pharmacy continues to fill it, and any refills the prescription itself allows, are between you and your pharmacy under pharmacy rules; UNZIT will not monitor your treatment, adjust doses, or answer treatment messages after your subscription ends.

2. On the All-In plan, Vida ships only while your subscription is active through the end of your paid period. No new prescriptions are written and no new shipments are made after that.

3. Ending your subscription ends your care relationship with UNZIT going forward. Arrange continuing care with another clinician, and remember the standing rule from your consents: if you have any side effect, stop the medication and seek care promptly; do not restart a stopped medication without a clinician's direction.

4. Your health record is kept as described in the Privacy Notice, and your rights in that notice continue after your subscription ends.

9. Changes to these terms

We may update these Subscription Terms. If we make a material change, we will notify you by email or in the app before the change takes effect where required, and the version you accept will be recorded. Changes do not alter a paid period already in progress.

10. Contact

Questions about billing or these terms: hello@tryunzit.com.

11. Your agreement

By selecting I AGREE at checkout, you agree to these Subscription Terms, including automatic monthly renewal until you cancel, and you confirm that you meet the eligibility requirements in section 3. I AGREE.

eligibilityQuestions.prompt: Welcome to UNZIT. UNZIT is online acne care from Dr. Amit Om, a board-certified dermatologist. Here is how it works. You answer questions and send photos of your skin. Dr. Om reviews everything himself, usually within 1 to 2 business days, and sends you a treatment plan. If prescription medicine is right for you, he sends it to your pharmacy. UNZIT is not for emergencies. If you ever have an emergency, call 911. Sometimes the safest care is in person. If Dr. Om thinks you need to be seen in person, he will tell you, and he may not prescribe. This visit takes about 10 minutes. You can save and come back.
What is your date of birth?
Are you physically in North Carolina right now? UNZIT can only treat you while you are in North Carolina, because that is where Dr. Om is licensed.
What do you want help with?

steps.title: Best for
steps.instructions: mostly blackheads and whiteheads.

steps.title: Morning
steps.instructions: gentle cleanser; moisturizer; SPF 30+.

steps.title: Evening
steps.instructions: Tretinoin 0.025%, pea-sized, every other night for 2 weeks, then nightly; moisturizer. If very sensitive, start 2 to 3 nights a week for the first 2 weeks, then every other night, then nightly.

steps.title: Prescription directions
steps.instructions: tretinoin 0.025%, sig "pea-sized, every other night x 2 weeks, then nightly; if very sensitive, start 2 to 3 nights a week and build up as tolerated."

steps.title: Treatment rules
steps.instructions: Clindamycin never without BPO. Doxycycline never alone: use with BPO and a topical retinoid, which continue after doxycycline stops. Do not start tretinoin and hydroquinone in the same week; add the other after 2 weeks. Use one retinoid at a time; remove OTC retinol and adapalene.

steps.title: Side effects and contact
steps.instructions: If you notice any side effect, even a small one, stop that medication and message us. Do not restart it until Dr. Om replies. Review within 1 to 2 business days. Not for emergencies. If you have trouble breathing, swelling of your face or throat, chest pain, or another emergency, call 911.

steps.title: Hydroquinone course and warning
steps.instructions: Hydroquinone is prescribed in courses of up to 12 weeks of once-nightly use, then stop and reassess. Do not use it continuously for longer than 12 weeks. exitPages.A: Stop here: your skin needs in-person care today. The symptoms you selected can be a sign of a severe form of acne that becomes dangerous quickly and cannot be treated safely online. Please go to urgent care or see a dermatologist today. If you feel very unwell, have a high fever, or your symptoms are getting worse fast, go to an emergency department or call 911. You have not been charged. Dr. Om will see the answers you gave today and will review them today, but please do not wait for that review to get care in person.
exitPages.B: Stop here: what you described needs urgent in-person care, not online care. Swelling of the face, lips, or eyes, or skin that is painful, blistering, or peeling, can be a sign of a serious reaction or infection. Please go to urgent care or an emergency department now. If you have trouble breathing or your throat feels tight, call 911. You have not been charged.
exitPages.C: UNZIT is for adults 18 and older, so we cannot treat you yet. Acne in your teens is very treatable, and a parent or guardian can help you find in-person care, or care designed for teens. You have not been charged.
exitPages.D: UNZIT can only treat patients who are physically in North Carolina, because that is where Dr. Om is licensed. If you will be in North Carolina, you are welcome to come back and start then. You have not been charged.
exitPages.E: UNZIT treats acne only, so it is not the right place for this concern. Rashes, eczema, moles, changing spots, and hair or scalp problems need in-person care, where a dermatologist can examine and test the skin directly. Please do not delay in-person care for anything that is new, changing, or worrying. You have not been charged.
